US-119-HR1829.title: Apache County and Navajo County Conveyance Act of 2026
US-119-HR1829.summary:
Apache County and Navajo County Conveyance Act of 2025

This bill requires the Forest Service to convey certain lands within the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest to Navajo County and Apache County, Arizona. The counties must use the land as cemeteries.

As a condition of each conveyance, the counties must pay all associated costs, including the costs of surveys and environmental analyses.

US-119-S4928.title: COVID–19 Commuter Benefits Distribution Act
US-119-S4928.summary:
COVID-19 Commuter Benefits Distribution Act

This bill allows a one-time withdrawal of certain unused amounts in an employee transportation fringe benefit account. (Conditions apply.)

As background, an employer may provide qualified transportation fringe benefits (e.g., transit passes and parking) to employees through a compensation reduction agreement, under which the employee designates a portion of their compensation for such benefits. Under current law, the amount designated under such an agreement (1) is excluded from the employee’s gross income (for federal tax purposes), up to a maximum monthly amount; and (2) may be used only for qualified transportation expenses.

Under the bill, an employee may withdraw unused amounts from a qualified transportation fringe benefit account, established through a compensation reduction agreement, without any conditions being placed on the use of such amounts. Only one withdrawal is allowed. Further, the withdrawal
• must occur within a specified period of time;
• may not exceed the highest balance in the employee’s transportation fringe benefit account during the period beginning on March 13, 2020, and ending on December 31, 2023; and
• must be included in the employee’s gross income.

US-119-S4928.aiSummary: The bill would let an employee take one one-time withdrawal of unused money from a commuter benefit account, if the account was set up through a pay cut agreement. The money could be taken out without rules on how it is used, but only within a set time and only up to the highest balance the account had from March 13, 2020, through December 31, 2023. The withdrawn amount would count as income for federal tax purposes.

US-119-HR9090.title: Advancing Menopause Care and Mid-Life Women’s Health Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9090.description: To improve menopause care and mid-life women's health, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9090.aiSummary: The bill would direct federal health agencies to expand research on menopause and mid-life women’s health, including symptoms, related conditions, and care methods. It would also create public health education and outreach efforts, along with grants and training to improve care and treatment for women going through perimenopause, menopause, and postmenopause. It authorizes $25 million each year from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for research, and $10 million each year from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for public health activities.

US-119-HJRES105.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "North Dakota Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan".
US-119-HJRES105.summary:
This joint resolution nullifies the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan (RMP) for the North Dakota Field Office and issued on January 8, 2025.

By way of background, an RMP guides the management of lands administered by BLM. The 2025 North Dakota RMP modified the 1988 RMP, including by limiting development of oil and gas in low-potential areas and new coal leasing to areas within four miles of existing mines.
US-119-HJRES105.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-07-10)

US-119-S160.title: Aerial Firefighting Enhancement Act of 2025
US-119-S160.summary:
Aerial Firefighting Enhancement Act of 2025

This act reauthorizes the Department of Defense to sell its excess aircraft and aircraft parts that are acceptable for commercial sale for wildfire suppression purposes. Such authority begins June 12, 2025, and ends October 1, 2035.

The act also provides that such aircraft may be used to deliver water by air in order to suppress wildfire (the previous authority only provided for the delivery of fire retardant).

The act removes the previous limitation on providing international wildfire suppression assistance with such purchased aircraft.
